label: attack-6-graveyard_attacker
system:
You are one member of a red team. You have been given ONE attack surface and you may not stray from it. You have not seen the author's reasoning and you do not want to; you see only the idea and the evidence.

Your job is to kill the idea on your surface. A weak attack wastes everyone's time. If your surface genuinely does not apply, say so with verdict "abstain" rather than inventing a weak objection; an abstention is not a survival.

Output JSON only.
user:
YOUR SURFACE — graveyard_attacker:
This already died. Find the closest dead product and argue the cause of death has not been dissolved.

IDEA
{
  "id": 6,
  "title": "House File",
  "unlock": "A vision-capable model now runs on the phone itself at zero marginal cost and offline, and a solo developer under two million lifetime downloads pays no cloud API fee at all, so identifying equipment from a photo costs nothing per look-up.",
  "pain": "Standing in front of an unfamiliar water heater or valve is a moment people have always handled by taking a blurry photo and asking someone later, and every product built for that moment so far was either an expensive single-purpose box with no market at the volume it needed [62] or one of hundreds of interchangeable apps that never found a channel [63].",
  "audience": "first-time landlords with a single rental unit",
  "mechanic": "capture_and_answer",
  "wedge": "Photograph three things in one unit - the main shutoff, the water heater label, the breaker panel - and get back a named, dated record of what is installed and which parts fit it.",
  "moat": "accumulated_personal_corpus",
  "model": "freemium_subscription",
  "loop": "professional_recommendation",
  "kill": [
    "On-device identification of common domestic fixtures from a phone photo is correct on fewer than 80 of 100 blind test shots taken by non-experts in bad light.",
    "Fewer than 3 in 100 free accounts pay within 60 days of their first saved photo.",
    "Fewer than 15 of 50 plumbers and electricians shown the finished record hand it on to a customer unprompted within 4 weeks.",
    "Blended cost per active user per month exceeds $0.30 once photos that fall back to cloud inference are counted."
  ],
  "why_not_obvious": "The obvious pitch to a landlord is rent collection or tenant messaging software, not a photographic inventory of pipework, because nobody thinks of a shutoff valve as a record worth keeping until the second time they need it.",
  "why_now": "The look-up that used to cost a cloud round trip per photo now runs free on the landlord's own phone [1][2], so the single-purpose device that had to carry that cost [62] is no longer the only way to deliver the answer."
}



Return JSON:
{
  "surface": "graveyard_attacker",
  "attack": "your strongest specific argument, 2-4 sentences, concrete",
  "strongest_defence": "the best answer the author could give",
  "verdict": "fatal" | "wounded" | "survived" | "abstain",
  "verdict_reason": "one sentence"
}

Use "fatal" only when the defence cannot work at all, because a fatal verdict
kills the idea outright and no other score overrides it. Use "wounded" when the
idea survives but is materially weaker. Use "survived" when your surface is
genuinely well answered.
